The Ultimate Guide to EV Charger Installation and Infrastructure in Los Angeles

Everything You Need to Know About EV Chargers and Their Infrastructure

As electric vehicles (EVs) continue to become more popular, the demand for efficient and reliable charging infrastructure is higher than ever. At Shaffer Construction, Inc., we specialize in installing EV chargers and the necessary infrastructure to ensure that your transition to electric is as smooth as possible. Below, we delve into the current state of EV charging infrastructure, the challenges being faced, and what we offer to help you stay ahead of the curve.

The Growing Demand for EV Chargers

With more automakers pivoting towards electric vehicles, it’s no surprise that the demand for EV chargers is skyrocketing. The global shift to electric vehicles, including both personal and fleet use, has picked up speed in recent years. This surge has led to a considerable strain on existing power infrastructure and significant challenges for charging station providers trying to keep pace with the growing need. Read more on the global transition to EVs here.

Incentives from Major Automakers

Understanding that the availability of reliable EV charging is vital for their sales, some automakers have introduced programs to support new EV owners. For instance, Ford has launched the Ford Power Promise initiative, which includes complimentary home chargers and free installation for new electric vehicle buyers or leasers. This move is designed to eliminate one of the primary barriers to EV adoption—home charging access. Learn about Ford’s new initiative here.

Challenges in the EV Charging Space

Despite the advances, the journey to seamless EV charging isn’t without hurdles. One significant issue that has surfaced is vandalism, particularly the theft of copper from charging units. This not only creates a financial burden on charging station providers but also disrupts service for consumers, deterring potential EV buyers. Discover more on the challenges faced by EV charging providers.

Public Charging Stations on the Rise

Investments in public charging stations are also gaining momentum. Retailers and service stations, like Kwik Trip, are adding EV charging points to their locations. These stations aim to serve the growing number of EV drivers who need accessible and reliable options on the road. This trend indicates that the infrastructure is gradually expanding to meet the needs of both private and commercial EV users. Read more about Kwik Trip’s EV charging initiatives.
